subject: Geography
description: Seven Sisters + Sikkim — capitals, statehood years, tribes, geography

questions.stem: The 'Seven Sisters' of North-East India are Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland and:

options.option_text: Sikkim
Tripura
West Bengal
Bhutan

questions.explanation: The 'Seven Sisters' coined by journalist Jyoti Prasad Saikia (1972) refers to Assam, Arunachal, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland and Tripura. Sikkim was added to the NE Council in 2002 — popularly called the 'brother' of the Seven Sisters. Together, they are the 8 NE states. Total area: ~262,000 km² (8% of India); population ~46 million (~3.8%). Border with 5 countries: China, Bhutan, Myanmar, Bangladesh, Nepal.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: Three NE states attained full statehood on the same day — 21 January 1972. They are:

options.option_text: Manipur, Tripura, Meghalaya
Mizoram, Arunachal Pradesh, Sikkim
Assam, Nagaland, Manipur
Manipur, Sikkim, Mizoram

questions.explanation: 21 January 1972 — Manipur, Tripura and Meghalaya all became full states (NE Areas Reorganisation Act, 1971). Earlier Manipur and Tripura were UTs; Meghalaya was carved out of Assam (autonomous state in 1970, then full state). Other NE statehood dates: Nagaland — 1 Dec 1963 (first to break away from Assam); Sikkim — 26 Apr 1975 (36th amendment); Arunachal Pradesh and Mizoram — 20 Feb 1987 (same day).
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The capital of Arunachal Pradesh is:

options.option_text: Itanagar
Aizawl
Kohima
Imphal

questions.explanation: Arunachal — Itanagar (named after Ita Fort, Bhalukpong fort built ~14th-15th century). Mizoram — Aizawl. Nagaland — Kohima. Manipur — Imphal. Other NE capitals: Assam — Dispur (within Guwahati); Meghalaya — Shillong (was the capital of undivided Assam till 1972); Tripura — Agartala; Sikkim — Gangtok. Itanagar's IATA airport is HJX (Donyi Polo Airport, opened Nov 2022).

questions.stem: India's only Salt Lake (a UNESCO Ramsar site) is in which NE state?

options.option_text: Manipur
Sikkim — Tso Lhamo / Gurudongmar
Loktak Lake — but it's freshwater
None — there is no salt lake in NE India; Sambhar (Rajasthan) is India's largest

questions.explanation: India's largest inland salt lake is Sambhar in Rajasthan, NOT in NE India. NE has many freshwater lakes — Loktak (Manipur, largest in NE), Tsomgo / Changu (Sikkim, glacial), Gurudongmar (Sikkim, sacred), Umiam (Meghalaya, man-made hydropower lake), Dawki / Umngot (Meghalaya, crystal-clear). Trap option: this question tests recall of 'salt lake' specifically — none exist in NE.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: Mawsynram — recognised as the wettest place on Earth — is in:

options.option_text: Mizoram
Meghalaya
Assam
Arunachal Pradesh

questions.explanation: Mawsynram (East Khasi Hills, Meghalaya) records ~11,872 mm of average annual rainfall — Guinness World Records confirms it as Earth's wettest. Cherrapunji (10 km away) was the previous holder. The hills act as a barrier to monsoon clouds rising over the Bay of Bengal, forcing them to dump moisture. State capital Shillong is also in the same district. 'Meghalaya' = 'abode of clouds' in Sanskrit.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The 'Apatani' tribe — famous for nose plugs and elaborate facial tattoos (now discouraged) — lives in which Indian state?

options.option_text: Nagaland
Arunachal Pradesh — Ziro Valley
Manipur
Sikkim

questions.explanation: Apatani tribe inhabits the Ziro Valley (Lower Subansiri district) of Arunachal Pradesh. Famous for distinctive face tattoos (younger women no longer practice; tradition was meant to make them less attractive to raiders), nose plugs (yapping hullo), and innovative paddy-cum-fish cultivation. The Ziro Valley itself is on UNESCO's tentative list. Apatani is one of ~26 major tribes of Arunachal — others include Adi, Galo, Mishmi, Nyishi, Monpa.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: Among the eight NE states, which one borders the highest number of other Indian states?

options.option_text: Assam — 7 Indian states
Manipur — 4 Indian states
Mizoram — 5 Indian states
Nagaland — 6 Indian states

questions.explanation: Assam shares inter-State borders with 7 Indian states: Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram, Tripura, Meghalaya and West Bengal — every NE state except Sikkim. International borders with Bhutan and Bangladesh. Assam's central location is why earlier 'undivided Assam' covered most of NE before progressive carve-outs (Nagaland 1963, Meghalaya 1972, Mizoram 1987, Arunachal 1987). Manipur borders 3 (Nagaland, Mizoram, Assam); Mizoram 3 (Assam, Tripura, Manipur); Nagaland 3 (Assam, Arunachal, Manipur).

questions.stem: Kaziranga National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site renowned for the Indian one-horned rhinoceros, lies along the southern bank of which river?

options.option_text: Barak River, which drains the southern valleys of Assam
Brahmaputra River, flowing through the heart of Assam
Subansiri River, originating in the hills of Arunachal Pradesh
Kopili River, a major south-bank tributary of the Brahmaputra

questions.explanation: Kaziranga straddles the floodplains of the Brahmaputra in Assam's Golaghat and Nagaon districts. The seasonal flooding of the Brahmaputra actually sustains the park's grassland ecosystem. The Barak is a separate river system in southern Assam with no connection to Kaziranga.

questions.stem: The bamboo folk dance 'Cheraw' — in which performers step rhythmically between pairs of moving horizontal poles — is the most celebrated indigenous dance of which NE state?

options.option_text: Nagaland, which showcases tribal dances at the Hornbill Festival
Manipur, home of classical Lai Haraoba and Sankirtana traditions
Mizoram, where Cheraw is performed at harvest and festive occasions
Meghalaya, celebrated for the Garo Wangala drum-dance festival

questions.explanation: Cheraw (also called the bamboo dance) is the iconic folk dance of the Mizo people of Mizoram. Performers step in and out of bamboo poles clapped together by seated players. Manipur is often confused here because of its rich dance heritage, but Sankirtana and Lai Haraoba are Manipuri, not Mizo traditions.

questions.stem: India's only floating national park — where the critically endangered Sangai deer roams on mat-like biomass islands — is located in which NE state?

options.option_text: Assam, along the seasonally flooded Brahmaputra floodplains
Nagaland, in the high-altitude grasslands near the Kohima district
Manipur, on the floating phumdis of Loktak Lake
Tripura, within the Sepahijala Wildlife Sanctuary reserve area

questions.explanation: Keibul Lamjao National Park in Manipur is the world's only floating national park, established on the phumdis (heterogeneous mass of vegetation and organic matter) of Loktak Lake. The Sangai (brow-antlered deer) exists nowhere else. Loktak Lake itself is a Ramsar-listed wetland. Assam is the common wrong answer because of its floodplain geography, but it has no floating park.

questions.stem: Which Article of the Indian Constitution grants special protection to Nagaland's customary law, religious practices, and traditional village administration, preventing Parliament from overriding them without the state legislature's approval?

options.option_text: Article 370, which earlier granted special autonomy provisions
Article 371A, exclusively designed for Nagaland's tribal traditions
Article 371C, which protects Manipur's Hill Area Committee functions
Article 371B, relating to Assam's Tribal Area representation in legislature

questions.explanation: Article 371A was inserted by the 13th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1962, specifically for Nagaland. It protects Naga customary law and village administration from Parliament's legislation unless the state assembly consents. Article 370 is the most common wrong answer (it related to J&K and has since been abrogated), while 371C protects Manipur's Hill Area Committee — a distinct provision.

questions.stem: Muga silk — famous for its natural golden sheen and GI-tagged to Assam — is produced by which silkworm species that feeds exclusively on the leaves of Som and Soalu trees?

options.option_text: Bombyx mori, the mulberry silkworm used in mainstream commercial sericulture
Antheraea mylitta, the tropical tasar silkworm found in central Indian forests
Philosamia ricini, which produces the creamy eri silk across northeast India
Antheraea assamensis, a semi-wild silkworm endemic to Assam's forest belt

questions.explanation: Antheraea assamensis is the silkworm unique to Assam that feeds on Som (Machilus bombycina) and Soalu (Litsaea polyantha) leaves, producing the rare golden Muga silk. Muga holds a GI tag and is one of the strongest natural silks. Antheraea mylitta produces tasar silk from central India — a common confusion because both belong to the same genus Antheraea. Eri silk (Philosamia ricini) is also produced in Assam but is white, not golden.

questions.stem: The Tawang Monastery in Arunachal Pradesh — the largest monastery in India — belongs to the Gelug school of Tibetan Buddhism. Which of the following correctly identifies a defining characteristic of the Gelug school?

options.option_text: It was founded by Padmasambhava and is regarded as the oldest surviving Tibetan school
It follows Je Tsongkhapa's reforms, emphasising strict monastic discipline and logical study
It was established by Marpa and Milarepa, centred on secret oral transmission lineages
It was founded in the 11th century in the Sakya region of Tibet by Khon Konchog Gyalpo

questions.explanation: The Gelug school (Yellow Hat) was founded by Je Tsongkhapa (1357–1419) and is the school of the Dalai Lamas. It is distinguished by its emphasis on strict monastic vinaya discipline and systematic philosophical study (Lamrim). Tawang Monastery was built in the 17th century under the patronage of the 5th Dalai Lama. Option A describes the Nyingma school (founded by Padmasambhava), C describes the Kagyu school, and D describes the Sakya school — all real Tibetan Buddhist schools used as precise distractors.

questions.stem: Manipur was brought under the Inner Line Permit (ILP) regime in December 2019. Which of the following lists ALL four NE states under the ILP system as of 2020?

options.option_text: Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Mizoram, and Sikkim (added under 2019 order)
Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Manipur, and Meghalaya (demand granted 2019)
Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Mizoram, and Manipur (added December 2019)
Arunachal Pradesh, Mizoram, Tripura, and Manipur (eastern border states)

questions.explanation: The ILP (under the Bengal Eastern Frontier Regulation, 1873) originally applied to Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, and Mizoram. Manipur was added on 11 December 2019 via a Presidential notification, partly driven by protests against the Citizenship (Amendment) Act. Sikkim (Option A) has its own Restricted Area Permit system but is not under ILP. Meghalaya (Option B) had strong ILP demands but was not formally included. Tripura (Option D) has no ILP requirement.
